claims: C1 the assistant may share its identity and capabilities
C2 the assistant must keep the underlying system or developer prompts private by default
C3 the underlying system or developer prompts may be disclosed only when policy explicitly allows it
C4 the analogy to a customer-service agent and training manual illustrates the same distinction: the manual equips the agent but is not disclosed unless policy allows

concepts.name: privileged_information_categories
concepts.gloss: C is a category of information that counts as privileged information, so that its disclosure is restricted

concepts.name: system_message_disclosure_distinction
concepts.gloss: D is a fact about the assistant's identity, capabilities, or tools that is shareable, as opposed to verbatim text or full details of the underlying prompts, which are not

concepts.name: underlying_prompt
concepts.gloss: P is one of the underlying system or developer prompts that constitute the assistant's instructions

concepts.name: policy_allows_disclosure
concepts.gloss: policy explicitly allows the disclosure of P
concepts.inference: the clause says disclosure is allowed only when policy explicitly allows it, so a predicate for that permission is needed

concepts.name: shareable_fact
concepts.gloss: F is a fact about the assistant's identity or capabilities that the assistant may share
